messages:
samir: Heads-up: RFC asked us to pick an admission policy for staging vs compact pools. I ran a short sim and have some wild results to share before we lock defaults.

zoe: Quick summary of constraints? trying to balance produced fragmentation vs p95 allocation latency?

samir: Exactly. Our target is <60ms alloc p95 on the small-hot path, while keeping node-level fragmentation <18% on average. Staging is fast for lonely large pages but fragments the global address space.

kevin: My read: we need an admission control that's size + age aware. Size-only rules are too crude for mixed workloads (e.g. many medium allocations that die quickly).

hanna: What about a token-bucket per-tenant + age histogram? New allocs get tentatively admitted to staging if size >= X OR age_hint==ephemeral. Token cost = size/MB rounded up. Tokens refill at R per minute.

samir: I like that. Add an emergency backstop: if staging_free_ratio < 0.15 then temporarily increase token cost multiplier (x2) and route new allocs to compact. Helps cut overcommit.

kevin: Also add an admission override for latency-critical routes. We can attach route_priority on allocation calls. High-priority bypasses token check but increments a separate fast-path counter and triggers fast-reclaim if > threshold.

zoe: Telemetry we'll need: staging_free_ratio, tenant_staging_tokens, fastpath_allocs, compaction_cpu_pct, migration_queue_len, alloc_latency_bucket. Example PromQLs:

# staging free ratio
sum(node_staging_free_bytes) / sum(node_staging_total_bytes)

# tenant token usage
sum(tenant_staging_tokens_used) by (tenant_id) / sum(tenant_staging_tokens_limit) by (tenant_id)

# fastpath alloc p95
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(allocator_fast_alloc_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

kevin: Implementation sketch for runtime flags (canary):

```
allocator: {
  policy: "token-age-hint",
  size_threshold_bytes: 131072,
  token_refill_per_min: 120,
  token_cost_per_mb: 1,
  emergency_staging_floor: 0.15,
  fastpath_override_limit_per_min: 50
}
```

hanna: Migration design: when a compact-first alloc happens because tokens exhausted, we enqueue async migrate task to attempt moving back to staging when free capacity returns. Migrations must be priority-low and cancelable if eviction pressure increases. Also cap concurrent migrations per node (default 8).

samir: For safety add: if migration failure rate > 10% over 10m, throttle migrations by 50% and escalate alert. Also add a rollback gate on canary if alloc_p95 jumps > 20% or compaction_cpu_pct > 30%.

infra-bot: canary deployed: policy=token-age-hint on zone-west-1 (20 hosts).

zoe: Testing plan: one-week canary with synthetic noisy-tenant (ramp to 5x typical token consumption) plus natural traffic. Compare baseline vs canary for: alloc_p95, staging_frag_ratio, compaction_cpu_seconds, tenant_throttle_events.

kevin: Add unit/e2e tests for token accounting edge cases (clock skew, restart, burst refill). Also test route_priority starvation scenarios.

hanna: I'll own migration queue + cancel semantics. Will instrument cancel reasons for debugging.

samir: I'll write the follow-up RFC with default values and the kill-switch. We should schedule a short sync after 48h of canary to review metrics.

zoe: +1. Leave this thread for the sync notes.
